summary: Charity Hub end-to-end test (backend + frontend). Backend 27/27 pytest pass: auth gating (401/403), non-admin submissions land pending, admin submissions auto-approve, public list returns only approved with search/category/state filters, pending detail visibility restricted to submitter/admin, claim flow idempotent + 409-on-other-claimed, contact records persisted, admin approve/reject and claim-approval-supersedes-others all work, duplicate (name+city) prevention returns 409, validation errors at 422. Frontend (Expo web preview, 390x844, admin + non-admin sessions minted via Mongo + injected into localStorage): all navigation entry points work (Home tile quick-charities, Community header community-charities-btn, Profile admin profile-admin-charities-link). /charities list loads & searches, /charities/submit submits to API successfully (POST 200), /charities/[id] renders with i-am-interested-btn, Interest modal sends and shows a custom Sent confirmation screen, /admin/charities renders Pending/Approved/Rejected/Claims tabs and approving moves a pending charity to Approved (POST .../approve 200). Non-admin correctly sees 'Admins only.' gate. One web-only UX bug: Alert.alert on the submit screen does not fire on react-native-web -> after a successful submission the user gets NO feedback and stays on the form (POST already succeeded). Several interactive elements (submit form inputs, approve/reject icon buttons in admin row) are missing testID props, making automated testing fragile.

ui_bugs.issue: Alert.alert success/error never appears on web. After POST /api/charities/submit returns 200 the user remains on the submit form with no feedback (router.replace inside Alert OK callback never runs because react-native-web's Alert.alert is effectively a no-op). Same risk for all error Alerts on this screen.

TextInput fields (name, mission, city, state, country, website, email, phone) and the bottom 'Submit for review' Pressable have no testID. Form-fill automation has to fall back to placeholder selectors.
Approve / Reject / Archive icon Pressables in each row have no testID and no accessibilityLabel. Hard to target without coordinate hacks.
Charity list rows (cards), the search TextInput, category chips, state filter, and back button have no testID.
Claim button, interest-modal textarea, 'Send interest' button, 'Done' button, and 'Submit claim' button have no testID. (i-am-interested-btn IS present.)

integration_issues.issue: Backend POST /api/charities/submit returns 200 (status pending or approved depending on role), but the web client never navigates back to /charities and shows no toast/alert. Result: a confused user may resubmit and hit the 409 duplicate guard.

action_items: Replace Alert.alert calls on /charities/submit (and any other web-facing flows) with either Platform.select to use window.alert/window.confirm on web, or a custom in-app toast/modal that runs the OK callback synchronously. Easiest fix: do router.replace('/charities') BEFORE Alert.alert so success-redirect works on both web and native.

Add testID props: submit-charity-name, submit-charity-mission, submit-charity-city, submit-charity-state, submit-charity-country, submit-charity-website, submit-charity-email, submit-charity-phone, submit-charity-button.
Add testID props on admin row buttons: admin-charity-approve-<id>, admin-charity-reject-<id>, admin-charity-archive-<id>, and the same for claim-row buttons.
Add testID props on /charities list: charity-search-input, charity-filter-toggle, charity-category-chip-<key>, charity-state-input, charity-card-<id>.
Add testID props on charity detail: charity-claim-btn, interest-modal-message, interest-modal-send, claim-modal-message, claim-modal-submit, interest-sent-done.
critical_code_review_comments: charity.py submit_charity duplicate detection: the city-regex branch uses `'$regex': f'^{re.escape(body.city)}$'` for the city only when body.city is provided; when city is empty, dup detection is skipped entirely. Consider also enforcing name-uniqueness within a country, otherwise two distinct submitters can create the same charity with no city.

charity.py admin_patch: when patching status to 'approved', `approved_by` / `approved_at` are NOT set (only the public approve endpoint does this). This will leave approved-via-patch charities with null approved_at, breaking the public list sort.

charity.py request_claim: claim_status is only marked 'pending' if the charity has no claimed_by yet; idempotent re-claim by same user does not refresh updated_at — fine, but admin dashboard may not surface it.
All endpoints use Depends(get_current_user) with no rate-limit or anti-spam on /submit or /contact — a logged-in user could spam contacts. Acceptable for Phase 1 but worth flagging.

_public_charity exposes `email`/`phone` on the public listing — confirm this is intentional (these are submitter-provided org contacts, but consider hiding on the public list response and only returning on detail).
seed_data_creation: Minted one admin session_token for user_ade7a898e281 and one non-admin test user (TEST_charity_uitest_*) with its own session for UI tests. All sessions, the test user, and any charity/claim/contact rows created with the TEST_QA_/QA_UI_/QA_NA_ prefix have been cleaned up. Pre-seeded admin user and real charities were NOT touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth is mintable: insert into user_sessions {session_token, user_id, expires_at} and on the web preview run localStorage.setItem('sanctus_session_token', JSON.stringify(token)) before navigating. RN-web Alert.alert is effectively a no-op for success callbacks; rely on either custom modals (the interest modal already does this correctly) or perform the side effect before showing the Alert. Approve/reject row icons in /admin/charities currently must be located by background color until testIDs are added.
rca_of_issue: Why Alert.alert OK-callback fails on web: react-native-web maps Alert.alert to a window.alert/confirm-style invocation that does not invoke the buttons array's onPress handlers when the dialog is dismissed (only the first button text is sometimes used as the message). Therefore `router.replace('/charities')` placed inside the success Alert's onPress is never executed. Reproduction: open /charities/submit on web preview, fill name + 10+ char mission, tap Submit; observe POST /api/charities/submit returns 200 but the form stays mounted and no toast/alert is visible. Mitigation: call router.replace('/charities') (and any state cleanup) outside the Alert.alert callback, or guard with Platform.OS === 'web' to use window.alert + immediate redirect.
